title: Cold-start PR minimizer and review scratchpad
content:
Context:
Quick personal scratchpad for reviewing PRs that cause cold-start regressions in the inference runtime. I want a reproducible, fast mini-playbook for triage + a minimal change path (PR minimizer) to reduce rollback surface. Mostly notes to self and a couple of heuristics to try when I’m alone on-call or pairing with someone for 20–40 minutes.

Goals:
- Rapidly determine whether a PR caused regression vs infra/noise (10–20m).
- Produce the smallest safe revert or targeted fix that restores baseline SLA.
- Capture follow-ups and low-effort mitigations to prevent recurrence.

Quick triage checklist (order matters):
1) Confirm signal: reproduce the spike with the same model/route/seq-len on a local or staging instance. If noisy, collect 3 runs.
   - Commands: ./scripts/bench-local --model=redwood-13b --seq=1024 --concurrency=1 --warmups=3 --samples=5
   - If latency distribution overlap > 15% vs baseline, flag as probable regression.
2) Check rollouts + canary config: was a variant deployed? did autopromote run?
   - Look at rollout history in Console (route -> rollouts).
3) Correlate with infra: node restarts, driver version bumps, kernel updates, GPU driver/ucode.
   - Use /observability/traces and infra events window +/- 30m.
4) Re-run with pinned kernels/quantization variant to see whether kernel selection change is the cause.
5) Bisect suspect commits if the change window is small (git bisect, local microbench reproducer).

Fast hypothesis shortcuts:
- If warmup token count increased in recent PRs (e.g., changed prefix handling), suspect KV cache cold starts.
- If perf regressed only at low concurrency, look at per-request overheads (serialization, RPC, context init).
- If perf regressed only at high concurrency, suspect batching/backpressure or queueing policy changes.

Minimal PR minimizer (how I shrink a PR down to isolate the broken bit):
- Create a branch off the PR: pr_minimizer/<pr>-shrink
- Revert hunks with the largest semantic surface first (config changes, new flags).
- Prefer toggles over rewrites: convert new code path into a runtime flag that defaults to old behavior, then flip in local to validate.
- Replace new allocs with stubs that mimic old allocations (avoid touching kernel code early).
- If the PR touches two subsystems (e.g., batching + cache), comment out the smaller one and run perf.
- Aim to produce a revert / targeted fix < 10 LOC where possible.

Observability checklist to attach to a PR review:
- Add latency histograms (P50/P95/P99) per-sequence-length bucket (<=128, 129–512, 513–1024, >1024).
- Add token-by-token timeline sampling (one in N requests) to catch slow-step regressions.
- Surface kernel selection logs per-request (which kernel chosen, heuristics used).
- Emit a small counter for "cold_kv_cache_miss" when first token path takes significantly longer.

Review heuristics (things I specifically look for in diffs):
- Hidden allocations on the hot path (new heap allocations inside the token loop).
- New logging or telemetry that does blocking I/O.
- Changes to default config values (timeouts, batcher windows, fallback thresholds).
- Unnecessary copies of model weights or large tensors on request path.
- New global locks or synchronized singletons that could serialize request handling.

Sample review note templates (copy into PR comments):
- "Small perf note: I see allocs introduced in token loop (line 234). Can we move allocation to init/worker pool?"
- "Can you add a perf test case in bench/ that reproduces this regression? I want to make this non-regression protected by CI."
- "Because this touches kernel selection, please add opt-in flag + rollout plan so we can A/B this safely."

Follow-ups & tech debt (quick capture):
- Add microbench harness that runs nightly against latest main to catch +alert for +10% P95 regressions. (owner: Rohan)
- Harden canary policy to keep 5% traffic pinned for 24h before autopromote (owner: S. Martinez).
- Create a small "safe-rollback" script that automatically reverts a rollout if P95 crosses threshold for >15m. (owner: me)
- Investigate whether protobuf serialization changed in deps pinned in PR (possible hidden perf cliff).

Notes-to-self / heuristics I forget: 
- Cold KV cache often shows as a long-tail single-token spike that disappears after first 1–3 requests.
- Prefetching tensors at route init helps but can increase memory; balance for Dedicated customers.
- When a PR touches both "compile" and "runtime" directories, the buggy surface is usually in the glue layer (kernel handshake).

Example quick reproduction script (local):
# (pseudocode in comment form)
1) checkout <commit>
2) ./scripts/launch-local-runtime --model redwood-13b --workers 2 --pin-kernel stable
3) python tools/request-sweep.py --seq-len 1024 --num 30 --concurrency 4 --report p95

When to escalate to SRE or oncall: 
- If reproducer shows higher p95 but the cluster also has OOMs or node flaps -> escalate immediately.
- If multiple models/routes affected across regions in same window -> operational incident.

Loose thoughts (brain dump):
- Could we add an automated "minimizer" job that takes a PR branch and attempts to revert hunks in parallel, running a canned microbench to find the smallest change that flips perf? Might be noisy but useful as a first pass.
- Consider enforcing a simple review checklist in GitHub that requires perf-risk items to be annotated (allocations, locks, default-change).
- Add a small "hotpath" test in CI that runs a 10s token loop and fails on any increase in wall time > 8%. Keep it lightweight so it runs on PRs.

Action log (short-lived):
- 2026-02-12: reproduced p95 regression on staging against pr/4821.
- 2026-02-13: created branch pr_minimizer/pr-4821-shrink, toggled new batching window -> no change.
- 2026-02-15: stubbed new telemetry -> small improvement; suspect blocking I/O in new logging path.
- 2026-02-20: paired with Rohan, produced targeted 6-line fix that moves a logger to async; running extended bench now.

Open questions:
- Is there a cheap way to surface kernel fallback frequency in the Console? Would help triage kernel-related regressions faster.
- How many PRs introduce allocs vs change config? Do we have historical breakdown? (Make a simple query against PR tags.)

End-of-doc: drop-in scratchpad for future quick runs and pairing sessions. Keep short notes here and move stable docs into shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime when finalized.

-- j.p."
